title: Safety-net refactor scratch
content:
Purpose: quick scratchpad for the "safety-net" refactor PR. Trying to capture: a lightweight review checklist, short refactor ideas that are cheap to iterate on, follow-ups (post-merge), and local repro/test steps. Keep this informal — notes to self and for reviewers.

Context:
- PR: runtime/serve: add safety-net fallback routing + compact kv-cache interface (see PR #5782).
- Motivation: reduce tail-latency regressions when large batches + quantized kernels cause OOMs; fallback to smaller model or reduced batch.
- Related tickets: JIRA RINF-2314 (safety-net design), RINF-2330 (batcher metrics gaps).

Quick review checklist (prioritize):
1) Safety: ensure fallback path never reads uninitialized KV cache. 
   - Check: initialization flags (cache_ready) and early-return conditions.
   - Look for: pattern "if (!cache_ready) return fallback" vs racey double-check.
2) Correctness: public API unchanged for callers (no new required args).
   - Confirm: no breaking changes to ServeRequest/ServeResponse structures.
3) Observability: surfaced metrics and traces for fallback events.
   - Required metrics: safetynet.fallback.count, safetynet.fallback.reason, safetynet.recovery.count
   - Required trace span: safetynet.fallback -> include original request id
4) Performance: microbench marks added and green.
   - Compare p50/p95 with and without fallback enabled.
5) Tests: unit tests + one integration simulating OOM path.
   - Unit: fallback triggers with mock kernel throwing OOMError.
   - Integration: small e2e with local quantized model and tiny GPU sim.
6) Docs: short console/UI blurb + config docs for fallback thresholds.
7) Security: ensure no new elevation of privileges; fallback uses same tenant context.
8) Rollback: can we flip feature flag remotely? Yes -> config flag "safetynet.enabled"

Cheap refactor ideas (low-risk, quick to land):
- Extract Batcher::maybe_fallback(RequestContext) into a small facade (BatcherFallback) so tests can stub it. Rationale: smaller diff for rollback and easier unit tests.
- Consolidate three copies of "reason" strings into an enum (FallbackReason) to avoid typos in metrics.
- Replace ad-hoc bool flags in CacheState with a single bitfield struct (CacheStateFlags) to make future additions easier.
- Add a tiny microbench harness under /bench/safetynet to run sequences of requests with toggleable kernel behaviors (OOM vs normal). Keep it disabled by default in CI.
- Move fallback config parsing out of startup into Config::loadFeatureToggles() so we can reload without restart in later PR.

Follow-ups (post-merge, prioritized):
P0 (within 1 sprint):
- Add canary rollout plan in console (product) with percentage controls. Owner: Ivy.
- Add regression alerts: if fallback.rate > 1% for 30m -> alert SRE. Owner: Rina.
P1:
- Add tight unit tests for serialized KV cache state to ensure recovery is idempotent. Owner: me (Noemi).
- Telemetry: sample the first 10 requests that trigger fallback and store anonymized prompts for eval. Owner: privacy review needed.
P2:
- Integrate fallback decisions into Optimize recommendations (so system can recommend quantization adjustments). Owner: product/optimize.

Example inline reviewer comments (copy/paste templates):
- "Nit: prefer enum FallbackReason::KernelOOM vs raw string here — easier to track in metrics."
- "Why not extract this into BatcherFallback? The function is 150 lines and mixes concerns (decide vs act)."
- "Please add an integration test that simulates OOM in the kernel and asserts fallback metric increments."
- "Add a short comment here about why we choose to drop KV cache vs reduce batch size for GPU mem pressure."

Risk matrix (quick):
- Regressions: medium — changes touch hot path in serving (batching). Mitigation: feature flag default off, staged rollout.
- Observability gaps: high risk for silent failures. Mitigation: require metrics and trace spans before merge.
- Performance cost: low/medium — fallback path should only run on error path; verify p50 unchanged.

Local repro & debug notes (how I validated during dev):
1) Start local runtime with small mem limit: ./scripts/run-local --gpu-mem=2G --config=tests/safetynet-config.yaml
2) Run bench harness: cargo run -p bench -- bin/bench_safetynet --concurrency=32 --send-size=512
3) To simulate OOM: set env KERNEL_SIM_OOM=1 or run with --kernel-fault=oom
4) Logs I check: stdout for "FALLBACK_TRIGGERED", metrics endpoint /metrics for safetynet.fallback.count
5) If you hit a deadlock on shutdown after fallback, likely cause: Batcher::flush() waiting on worker that aborted — see notes below.

Gotchas I ran into while coding (notes to self):
- Flaky test: test_fallback_recovers occasionally fails because mock kernel sends on a closed channel; need to add non-blocking send or channel buffer.
- Trace baggage lost on thread hop; made trace span a field on RequestContext to force propagation.
- Some models have very long KV entries; fallback that truncates cache must also update token offsets — subtle off-by-one bug.

Owner assignments quick map:
- Me (Noemi): finalize unit tests + KV idempotency tests, follow-up P1 items.
- Ivy: console canary + rollout docs.
- Rina: SLO/alerting rules, add to runbook.
- Luca: microbench harness + perf report.

TODO (short):
- [ ] Add enum FallbackReason and replace strings (small PR).
- [ ] Add BatcherFallback facade (split PR, land first).
- [ ] Write integration test simulating kernel OOM.
- [ ] Update docs in /docs/ops/safety-net.md (console blurb).
- [ ] Draft canary rollout steps in product doc (link to JIRA once created).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally split into two PRs: 1) small safety changes + metrics + tests 2) refactor extraction (BatcherFallback). If you prefer a single PR, we can bundle but risk larger review surface.
- If you want to run the microbench locally but don't have CUDA, use --kernel-sim to run a CPU-based simulation.

Scratch extra: sample tiny pseudo-code for fallback decision (for review):

// pseudo
// returns true if we should fallback for this request
fn should_fallback(ctx, cache_state, kernel_result) -> bool {
  if kernel_result == KernelError::OOM { return true }
  if cache_state.size > ctx.config.cache_max_tokens { return true }
  // temporary threshold for testing
  if ctx.metrics.recent_latency_p95 > ctx.config.latency_threshold { return true }
  false
}

End of doc — keep this as working notes. Will clean and move parts into PR description and product doc before merge.
